author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A read-only specialty directory page lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it by full name, on one page without pagination. The page is reached by its address alone.
acceptance_criteria: given the clinic's specialties, when GET /specialties.html is opened, then every specialty is listed by its stored name with the veterinarians holding it
given a veterinarian holding a specialty, when the specialty directory is opened, then that veterinarian is shown by full name, first name then last name (for example "Helen Leary")
given a veterinarian holding no specialty, when the specialty directory is opened, then that veterinarian appears under no specialty
given any number of specialties, when the specialty directory is opened, then all of them render on one page without pagination
edge case 3: a specialty no veterinarian holds is still listed, shown as held by none
edge case 4: a veterinarian holding several specialties appears under each one
edge case 5: specialties, and the veterinarians under each, appear in a stable order rather than an arbitrary one

the page carries the standard navigation to owner search and the veterinarian directory (REQ-SYS-001), and all its new wording is present in every supported language with nothing hard-coded (REQ-LANG-002)
non_goals: managing veterinarians or specialties (NG-2 unchanged, per intake decision 1)
a navigation entry or a link from any other page to the specialty directory (intake decision 2; a possible follow-up request)
searching or filtering the specialty directory (NG-9 stands; the page is a listing, not a search)
listing veterinarians who hold no specialty
notes: Owner absent (intake line 1). NG-2 and NG-9 rows unchanged; no scope_overrides needed. Decided at scoping as the narrowest reading of 'every specialty', recorded as open questions in docs/prd.md: a specialty with no holder is listed as held by none; order is stable (specific ordering left to design). REQ-VET-003 is the next unused VET id (REQ-VET-002 withdrawn, never reused). REQ-LANG-002 wording parity is covered by the existing I18nPropertiesSyncTest; no new test name owed. author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Read-only page inside the vet feature package (system-design § Package Structure, ADR feature-package-organization), server-rendered (ADR server-side-rendering-with-thymeleaf). Existing patterns cover it with three small additions recorded in § Contracts: SpecialtyRepository mirrors PetTypeRepository (an ordered lookup query, Repository pattern); SpecialtyDirectory is an immutable record value object whose static pure factory inverts the Vet-to-Specialty association and fixes the order (architecture-principles § Logic Placement: a view model leaves the bean); SpecialtyDirectoryController is a thin web controller for GET /specialties.html. A new § Scale and Load section carries the page's row. Grep-based basis (IDE oracle not connected): VetController, VetRepository, Vet, Specialty, PetTypeRepository, templates/fragments/layout.html read directly. Distinct surface, so a new controller rather than a third route on VetController; the prd-entry's VetController file target is superseded by this placement.
integration_points: Entry point GET /specialties.html binds no request parameter: no form object, no @ModelAttribute, no @RequestParam; the handler loads, delegates to SpecialtyDirectory, and selects the view (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog, Web controller row).

Repository boundary, SpecialtyRepository: extend Repository<Specialty, Integer> (not JpaRepository) with the single ordered query, so the interface stays small enough to hand-double. The ordering query is verified against the real H2 seed in the existing @DataJpaTest suite (ClinicServiceTests), a real implementation.

Repository boundary, VetRepository: the controller reads the cached findAll() collection, unchanged. In SpecialtyDirectoryControllerTests both repositories are hand-written doubles registered as beans for @WebMvcTest (testing-principles § Mocking Policy: hand-write mocks first); a @MockitoBean stub is not named for this slice.
Framework transport: MockMvc drives the real MVC dispatch and Thymeleaf rendering (the one sanctioned mock, CLAUDE.md Testing Strategy).

Domain logic: SpecialtyDirectoryTests unit-tests the factory with real Vet and Specialty instances, no Spring context; the grouping, the held-by-none case, the multi-specialty case, and both orders are decided there, not in the controller.

Layout: the page uses fragments/layout with an active-menu value matching no navigation item, so the standard navigation renders (REQ-SYS-001) and no entry is added or highlighted (intake decision 2).

Wording: new message keys (page heading, veterinarians column) go into every messages*.properties bundle; reuse the existing 'specialties' and 'none' keys. I18nPropertiesSyncTest enforces REQ-LANG-002.

patterns.description: ordered lookup query on a persisted lookup value; SpecialtyRepository follows it
vet-package controller shape: package-private, constructor-injected repository, returns a vets/ view name
full-name rendering, the 'none' message key, and the layout fragment call

risks.risk: Instance-identity matching: Specialty inherits no value equality, and the cached Vet collection holds Specialty instances from an earlier load than the per-request specialty query, so grouping by object finds no holders.
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyDirectory matches holders to specialties by identifier (system-design § Contracts invariants; architecture-principles § Domain Core: reference by identity). A unit test builds the vet's specialty and the listed specialty as distinct instances sharing one id.

risks.risk: Order drift: VetRepository.findAll() guarantees no order and specialty names are not unique in the schema.
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyDirectory fixes the order: specialties by name then identifier; holders by last name, first name, then identifier (system-design § Contracts invariants). Do not rely on query or cache order for the holders.

risks.risk: Specialty directory page, an unpaged path that scales with specialties and veterinarians (system-design § Scale and Load, specialty directory row).
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form: in-memory grouping over the cached vet collection; no paging, no new cache.

risks.risk: Rule leaking into the controller (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog: a new controller rule is a fresh violation).
risks.mitigation: Grouping, held-by-none, and ordering live only in the SpecialtyDirectory factory; the controller holds two loads, one delegation, one view name.

risks.risk: Lazy-loading failure in the view with open-in-view disabled (system-design § Persistence).
risks.mitigation: Vet.specialties is eager and the template reads only the SpecialtyDirectory record's names; pass the record, not entities, to the model.

notes: Owner absent (intake line 1, owner_present false). Proceeded on durable memory and the narrowest reading of the intake decisions; no foundational signal trips (system-design populated and partly confirmed, ADRs record stack and shape, vocabulary populated, no new bounded context). No ADR: the choices are contained in this slice. No design-doc-autofix records to audit. Open for the owner, recorded not decided: the holder order (last name, first name) was chosen at design because the PRD left it open; proposed confirmation sentence for the owner, 'Within each specialty, veterinarians are listed by last name, then first name.' The held-by-none rendering and the deferred entry point remain the PRD's open questions. The Vet cache has no eviction (system-design Open Question 5); the page inherits that staleness.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListSpecialtiesByNameThenIdentifier cannot fail if the identifier tie-break (thenComparing(Specialty::getId) in SpecialtyDirectory) is removed. Both 'surgery' specialties are given no holders and the assertion extracts only names, so ['surgery','surgery'] is the result in either order, and the stable sort keeps the input order anyway. The test name claims a rule it does not pin down.
findings.fix: Give each same-named specialty a different holder (or otherwise a distinguishable Listing) and assert whole Listings with containsExactly, with the input order opposite to id order, so dropping the id tie-break fails the test. Use named ids and names instead of reusing RADIOLOGY_ID for a 'surgery' specialty.

findings.description: theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListVeterinariansByLastNameThenFirstNameThenIdentifier has the same flaw for vets. The two 'Ann Smith' vets (ids 2 and 3) render to the identical string 'Ann Smith', so the identifier tie-break is unobservable in the output. The test passes whether or not thenComparing(Vet::getId) exists. Last-name-then-first-name ordering is covered; the identifier part is not.
findings.fix: Remove 'ThenIdentifier' from the test name and the vet-with-equal-names rows, since the tie-break cannot be seen in the output. If the identifier order is a required contract, the output must expose something that differs between the two vets. Otherwise keep the last-name/first-name case only.

findings.description: The controller suite repeats SpecialtyDirectory's case table. SpecialtyDirectoryTests already decides grouping (:50), held-by-none (:82), multi-specialty (:91), and both orders (:104,:116). The controller tests theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListUnderEachSpecialtyTheVeterinariansHoldingIt (:134), ...ListAVeterinarianUnderEachSpecialtyTheyHold (:171), and ...InAStableOrder (:196) each rebuild a SpecialtyDirectory model to compare. ...ListNoVeterinarianWhoHoldsNoSpecialty (:154), ...ListASpecialtyNoVeterinarianHoldsAsHeldByNone (:162), and ...ShowEachVeterinarianByFirstNameThenLastName (:145) re-run the unit's grouping and held-by-none cases through rendering. testing-principles § Coverage: the client exercises a collaborator through one representative path per decision it makes. The controller's own decisions are two loads, one delegation, and one view name. coverage-map lists the same test names under both files for the held-by-none, no-specialty, and multi-specialty bullets. A change to the ordering or grouping rule would fail the unit test and these controller tests together.
findings.fix: Keep in the controller suite one test that the model carries the directory built from both repositories and the view name is vets/specialtyList, and one rendering test that a specialty name, a holder's full name, and the 'none' text appear. Merge ListEverySpecialty (:123) and RenderEverySpecialtyOnOnePage (:184) into the one rendering test. Delete the multi-specialty, order, no-specialty-vet, and first-then-last-name controller tests; the unit suite owns them.

findings.description: Construction (conventions-map rows: the controller suite has 3 raw 'new Specialty()/new Vet()' hits at :105,:112 and 8 further construction/literal rows including nested 'new SpecialtyDirectory.Listing(...)'; the unit suite has :33,:40 plus 'new SpecialtyDirectory.Listing' rows at :58,:69,:79,:88,:100-101). Two problems against testing-principles § Test Data Construction and § Three-Tier Data. (1) aSpecialty(int,String) and aVet(int,String,String,Specialty...) are copy-pasted into both suites as parameterised helpers. A named default takes no parameters and lives once. (2) Inline literals ('Helen','Leary','James','Carter','Linda','Douglas', ids 1..4, 'radiology') are filled in at call sites with no role names; in the 'no specialty' and 'many' tests they are irrelevant scaffolding (Tier 2) with no SOME_/ANY_ name. The existing vet fixtures in VetControllerTests (james(), helen()) were not reused.
findings.fix: Hold one shared test-side named default for an irrelevant Specialty and Vet (no parameters), and have tests apply setters or withers for the attribute that matters. Name meaningful values by role (e.g. HOLDER_FIRST_NAME). Remove the duplicate helper bodies. Reuse the existing helen()/james() style defaults where the vet is irrelevant.

findings.description: Fully qualified 'java.util.stream.IntStream' inline instead of an import, and the many-specialties assertion uses containsString("specialty-1<") which couples the test to the exact HTML closing tag after the name. 'MANY_SPECIALTIES = 12' is a Tier 1 name but nothing in the page makes 12 special; the no-paging bullet would be checked equally by comparing against the model.
findings.fix: Import IntStream. Assert the rendered page contains every generated specialty name, or the model size, rather than a tag-adjacent substring.
